records.reason: Useful constitutional baseline for presidential authority over defense and emergency powers, but it is formal authority rather than 2022 exercise.
Official biography only repeats office tenure and adds no 2022-specific substantive evidence beyond the constitutional baseline.
Direct 2022 executive step toward TPNW ratification; useful as process context, but the UN depositary record is the stronger legal proof.
Legislative passage repeats the same ratification track already covered by the executive bill and final depositary record.
Best direct legal evidence for the 2022 ratification date and entry into force.
NGO summary mirrors the same ratification facts already captured by the UN treaty record.
Post-period corroboration of the non-nuclear declaration, useful only as retrospective confirmation.
Authoritative legal-status record for safeguards and physical-protection treaty obligations in force in 2022.
Pre-Tshisekedi CTBT status establishes inherited treaty baseline, but it predates the period under review.
Older CTBTO notice is a predecessor-era duplicate of the CTBT ratification baseline.
Conference presidency on cybersecurity is indirect and does not materially bear on nuclear posture or ruler authority.
Shows a 2022-era cybersecurity policy instrument under the presidency, but it is adjacent rather than direct evidence for nuclear capability.
Direct presidential crisis speech helps establish general security posture and executive conduct in 2022, though it is not nuclear-specific.
Independent retrospective monitor adds useful non-nuclear corroboration on stockpiles and fissile-material absence, but it is not contemporaneous primary evidence.

remaining_concerns: Most direct evidence is legal and status-based rather than operational, so it supports non-nuclear posture more strongly than any exercised command capacity.
Several records are derivative, retrospective, or adjacent-topic corroboration, so the UN and IAEA records carry the most weight.
